evidence: The track is 211 cm long. It enters 14 cm below the top (y=592) and runs down to a fit end at (157.2, 468.7, 294.1) in APA3 (x>0, z>232). The dQ/dx plateau is 5.5-6e4. From s~20 it climbs along the muon curve to a peak of 1.23-1.3e5 (about 2.2x plateau) at s=4-5. It then collapses: one point at 5.6e4 at s=3, then five points at 2.2-3.9e4 (0.4-0.65x plateau, a factor 3-6 under the peak) over the last ~2.5 cm. That stretch is the chain s last segment 114004 (2.9 cm, 6 pts, 2.8e4). The c and e azimuths show a small kink at the 114003/114004 vertex. A muon at its Bragg peak cannot fall to half its plateau in its last centimetres. evidence: 333 cm straight track whose fit end is at (350.9, 446.2, 346.4), face.x 7.1 cm, i.e. |x| = 351 at the anode wire plane of APA3 (x>0, z>232); the chain entry end is at (145.3, 223.2, 443.9), 223 cm lower and 18 cm from the back face. The dQ/dx sits on a ~4-6e4 plateau; a 5-point bump to 0.7-1.06e5 at s=3-7 is followed by the last 3 cm back at 3.2-4.5e4, below the plateau, so the profile does not climb to the end along the muon curve: no clear rise, and no decay topology (nothing leaves the end in the three azimuths; 116004 straight ahead at 2-4 cm has no charge value, a degenerate row). The fit end is the upper end of the track, so a downward cosmic came in through the anode here and ran down to the lower end. f_meas shows clean charge to the end in all planes; the W dead band at ch ~9535 crosses the body 30 cm back, not the end. 117003 (3.6 cm at 30 cm back, on the body) is a delta ray: delta / other.

notes: ANODE: face.x 6.7 cm (|x| 351.3), profile falls toward the end; geometry is an anode entry for a downgoing muon exiting the front face
evidence: 53 cm; the chain entry is at the front face (z face 1.7 cm, y=418) and the fit end is at (-351.3, 460.0, 20.5): face.x 6.7 cm, i.e. |x| = 351.3, at the x<0 anode wire plane, 20 cm from the front face, in APA0. Not isochronous (|dx|/L = 0.25). The end sits 42 cm higher than the front-face end, so this reads as a downgoing muon that enters through the anode here and leaves through the front face. The APA0 profile is ragged (2.5-7.5e4 with dips to near zero at 29 and 40 cm), and toward the end it falls rather than rises: 2.5-4.5e4 over 4-8 cm and 0.5-1.5e4 over the last 3 cm. No rise at the anode end. No decay topology: 25004 is a 2.9 cm stub straight on (cos_fwd 0.95, 0.4 cm off axis) at ~1.0e4, a continuation into the anode, tagged muon as a THRU stub with charge; 24005 is a degenerate row (no dQ/dx): delta / other. All three azimuths show nothing else at the end. f_meas: U, V and W charge end at the low-time end (~slice 810, shortest drift), no dead band nearby. An end at the anode with no rise: THRU.

notes: Near-isochronous (x within 4 cm over 30 cm) with the end on a W dead band edge and a flat half-MIP profile; rule 3 excluded. Competing reading STM_ONLY from U/V charge ending.
evidence: 30 cm faint track; enters through the top (y=605.8, 0.2 cm) and the fit ends at (-345.6,581,275) in APA2, 24.7 cm below the top, 12.4 cm from the -x anode face, 44 cm from the APA seam and 343 cm from the cathode. It is near-isochronous: x runs only -349.4 to -345.6 over 30 cm (local x-component ~0.15), and the whole track sits in ~17 time slices (605-622) in f_meas, with only 92 image points. The dQ/dx profile is smooth and low, 1.5-3e4 along the whole length (about half the muon reference plateau), with a gentle wave and no climb at all over the last 20 cm; the smoothness and sparse imaging say this profile is poorly measured. The object table holds only the two fitted segments; nothing is drawn past the end in any azimuth, no arm, stub or speck. f_meas: the stop end sits right at the edge of a W dead band (ch ~8888), so the collection plane cannot say whether charge continues; U (which has a dead band mid-track at ch ~2085) and V show the track ending there with nothing beyond in the window. Rule 3 does not apply to a near-isochronous track, there is no rise and no decay topology, and the end coincides with a W dead band, so the reading is a track whose continuation is lost, not a stopper. Hard: U and V both show the charge ending, which on a non-isochronous track would make this a FLAT_STOP; a 100 MeV stopper entering from the top is also plausible.

notes: Near-isochronous top-to-back-face crosser; end 1.4 cm from the z=462 face. Medium only because of the isochronous clause; would otherwise be high.
evidence: 455 cm; enters through the top (y=604.8, 1.2 cm) at z=233 and the fit ends at (-55.4,286,460.9), 1.4 cm from the back face (z=462), 53 cm from the cathode and 230 cm from the APA seam, in APA2. The whole track is near-isochronous: x stays between -55 and -58 over 455 cm, and f_meas shows it as a horizontal line at slice ~380 across all three planes, crossing several U/W dead bands. The dQ/dx profile over the last 40 cm is smooth and wavy at 3-5e4 with a dip to ~0 at s=27 (an interpolation artefact of isochronous imaging), and it is flat at ~4.5e4 over the last 5 cm with no climb along the muon curve. Nothing sits past the end: the only non-chain row is 33012, a 1.7 cm pdg-11 speck at the top entry point 392 cm back (delta / other). In the stop azimuths the end is a clean track end with no arm; the dotted grey trace beside the track is the fit/image offset along the isochronous line, not a second object. The end is at a face with a flat profile, so this is a top-to-back-face crossing muon. Confidence is set to medium only because the rubric asks for medium/low on near-isochronous tracks; the exit itself is not in doubt to me.

notes: ANODE: fit end at face.x 6.4 cm, flat profile; the other end is on the front face, so the track crosses two faces
evidence: 37 cm corner-clipping track in APA0 (x<0, z<231) at y~507-518: the chain entry end is on the front face (z=0.7, 0.5 cm from it) and the fit end is at (-351.6, 507.0, 16.0), face.x 6.4 cm, i.e. |x| = 352 at the anode wire plane. Both ends are at faces. The dQ/dx is ragged (0.8-8e4, APA0 patchy collection) and the last few cm read 2-6.8e4 with no climb along the muon curve: no rise. Nothing leaves the fit end at an angle in the three azimuths; 47009 (3.2 cm, 1.5-2 cm out, no charge value) is a degenerate row. f_meas shows charge to the end in all three planes with no dead band there. A short track entering through the front face and leaving through the anode. The delta rays and the unassigned 202010 sit 16-22 cm back near the entry: delta / other.

notes: NO_MEASUREMENT: near-isochronous (x within 4 cm over 200 cm, parallel to V), APA0, smooth low profile with zeros; rule 3 excluded, only a collinear stub past the end. Leading alternative THRU (lost isochronous continuation), cf. owner isochronous THRU precedent.
evidence: 200 cm; the chain entry end is 3.9 cm above the bottom face (y=11.5, z=305) and the fit end is mid-volume at (-94.4,85,201) in APA0, 77 cm above the bottom, 30 cm from the APA seam, 92 cm from the cathode and 264 cm from the anode. The track is almost perfectly isochronous: x stays within -90 to -94 over 200 cm, f_meas draws it as a horizontal line at slice ~365-383, and it runs nearly parallel to the V wires, so V collapses it onto a few channels around 3500. The fit zig-zags in the 3-D views, a sign of isochronous imaging trouble. The dQ/dx profile is smooth and very low (0.5-3.5e4, a gap of zeros at s=9-11) with APA0 on top, so the last 20 cm carries no usable Bragg measurement. Past the end: only 53009, a 4.7 cm stub at 0-4 cm running straight on (cos_fwd 0.98, no kink), weak topology that I tag as muon continuation. 249007 is a 3.9 cm faint piece 44-48 cm back, ~22 cm off the body line, inside a sparse cloud of thinned context points (delta / other); 53006 is an attached arm 75-83 cm back on the body (delta / other). A large grey isochronous band of context charge at the same x crosses the detector ~235 cm above the stop. Rule 3 is excluded for a near-isochronous track, there is no rise to read and no decay topology, so neither a stop nor an exit can be established. Leading alternative: THRU, since the fit end is the upper end of a bottom-entering isochronous track and a lost continuation is the usual isochronous failure.

notes: Competing reading STM_MICHEL: muon stops at the kink ~10 cm back and the bent piece (dip then hot end) is the electron; no pin moved because the collapse precedes the peak rather than following it. 157001 gamma is a 2-point speck at 55 cm; its tag decides detached dots vs none.
evidence: 162 cm single segment; the chain entry end is near the top/-x anode corner (6.1 cm from the anode face, 10.4 cm below the top) and the fit end is mid-volume at (-264,466.5,292) in APA2, 94 cm from the anode, 139.5 cm below the top, 61 cm from the APA seam and 262 cm from the cathode. The last ~10 cm bends by roughly 30-40 deg away from the straight body (clear in all three stop azimuths). Profile: plateau ~5.5e4 over s=12-45 (single 7.7-8e4 points at s=19 and 31); a dip to 1.5-2.5e4 over s=4-11 in the bent section; then the last 3 cm climbs to 0.86-1.1e5, about 2x plateau, sitting right on the muon reference curve. f_meas shows why the dip is untrustworthy: the bent section runs at constant time (slice ~330-332) in U and W, a short near-isochronous piece, while V ends cleanly at the same slice; the charge ends in all three planes at the fit end with no dead band there and nothing continuing in the window. I read the end as the muon Bragg peak after a low-momentum end-of-range bend, with the dip an imaging artefact of the isochronous piece (sub-MIP charge is unphysical for either a muon or an electron). Nothing is drawn past the end: no stub or hot tip ahead (no undershoot). One 2-point, 0.4 cm speck 157001 sits 55 cm out at cos -0.82 but ~32 cm off the body line: isolated and inside 60 cm, so a capture gamma on an STM_ONLY. Hard: the bent 10 cm could instead be a Michel leaving a muon that stopped at the kink; I did not take that because there is no rise before the kink (s=11-20 is plateau) and the end shape follows the muon curve.

notes: kind hangs on three faint specks (2.7 cm at 40.6 cm; two 2-point specks at 58.5/58.7 cm, just inside the 60.0 edge); last ~3 cm of the profile slide from ~100k back to ~57k (not below plateau), pin left at fit end; W-only grey line starting near the stop does not match U/V slices
evidence: 590 cm chain. The upper end (-13.7, 431.6, 17.9) is 17.7 cm inside the front z face next to the cathode. The track crosses the cathode near z~50 and runs down to the fit end (147.4, 38.7, 366.2) in APA3. The fit end is 31 cm above the floor, 96 from the back face, 135 from the seam, 147 from the cathode and 205 from the anode, so it is not at any face or gap. It is the lower end (dy = -393 over a 549 cm chord), so rule 7 is satisfied. The dQ/dx plateau is ~55-65k over 20-45 cm (dips to ~35k at 30 and 41 cm). Over the last ~11 cm it climbs to ~85-100k, sitting on or above the muon curve at 3-10 cm, then the last ~3 cm ease back to ~57-72k. That is a rise, ragged, with the final few points sliding back to plateau rather than collapsing below it, so I left the pin at the fit end. A 4-point bump to ~95k at 16-18 cm means the end rise is not unique, which is why I say medium. The end hooks slightly in U (f_meas) and in one 3-D azimuth, as stopping-muon ends often do. Nothing is attached at the stop. In f_meas the track own charge ends in U, V and W. One single W dead channel crosses ~20 channels before the end without swallowing it. In W a grey line starts near the stop and runs off steeply to lower slices for ~110 slices; U and V have nothing at matching slices, so I read it as another object crossing in W, not a continuation. Past the stop: S290017, a 2.7 cm faint speck 40.6 cm out, well off the body line (cos_fwd -0.25), and two 2-point specks S287015 and S288016 at 58.5-58.7 cm. On an STM_ONLY these are isotropic capture-gamma candidates inside the 60 cm edge, so gamma.

notes: Busy stop: 180 cm overlapping cluster C29 lies on the body and continues ~30-45 cm past the fit end in 3-D. Competing readings: FRAG_THRU (C29 is the muon continuation), or FLAT_STOP STM_ONLY from f_meas (charge ends in all three planes, C29 past the end being ghost points).
evidence: 264 cm chain of 12 short fitted segments; the chain entry end is at the front face (z=4.1, 3.9 cm, y=252) and the fit ends at (-151.9,451,47.7) in APA0, 47.5 cm from the front face, 155 cm below the top, 149 cm from the cathode and 206 cm from the anode, so mid-volume. A second cluster, C29 (2648 points, 180 cm, no PR segment), lies along the whole muon body from 0.4 to 212 cm and, in all three stop azimuths, its sparse cloud carries on straight past the fit end by roughly 30-45 cm, to the frame edge. The muon profile is not a measurement: 1-2e4 over the whole last 30 cm (a quarter to a third of the reference plateau even allowing for the APA0 0.65 factor), smooth and wavy, with a single 6e4 bump at s=32; the charge appears shared with the overlapping cluster, and the diff panels in f_meas are pink along the track (measured above the fit prediction). f_meas shows the measured charge ending at slice ~1475 in U, V and W at the fit end with nothing beyond inside the window, which on its own would give a FLAT_STOP; but the long overlapping cluster that reaches past the end means I cannot isolate where this track ends or what leaves it. Rule 6 (a long cluster lying on the body at the end) applies. Also note the fit end is the upper end of the track (y=451 vs 252 at the front face), which fits C29 being the upward continuation that this cluster lost. All rows delta / other as required for MESSY.

notes: Competing reading STM_MICHEL if 110011/110013 (branching off the body ~10 cm upstream, 10-16 cm from the stop, cos ~-1) are taken as a backward Michel arm; I read them as delta rays because they do not start at the stop vertex.
evidence: 153 cm; enters through the top (y=605.8, 0.2 cm) and the fit ends mid-volume at (206.8,494,292) in APA3, 112 cm below the top, 151 cm from the anode, 204 cm from the cathode and 61 cm from the APA seam. Strong Bragg rise: plateau ~5.5-6.5e4 over s=15-45, a dip to 3.3-4.5e4 at s=7-14, then the last segment 110004 (8.7 cm, 1.5e5 average) climbs through 8.5e4 (s=6) and 1.2e5 (s=5.5) to 1.43-1.75e5 over s=0-4, i.e. 2.5-3x plateau on the muon curve. The last point (1.43e5) is ~18% under the peak at s~3.5: ordinary scatter, not a collapse, so the pin stays. Nothing lies past the end: every other row sits behind the stop (cos_fwd -0.97 to -1.0) and f_meas shows no charge beyond slice ~635 in any plane, no dead band at the end. No hot tip ahead (no undershoot). Behind the stop: 110010 (2.6 cm at 7.7-10 cm) hugs the body; 110011 (7.5 cm, faint 6.7e3) and 110013 (3.8 cm, 2.7e4) leave the body at an angle from a point ~10 cm upstream of the stop and reach 13-16 cm out, so they branch off the muon body rather than start at the stop vertex: delta rays, delta / other; 110009 is a 10 cm arm dropping off the body 20-23 cm back, also a delta ray. Hard: 110011/110013 start right at the ~10 cm radius inside which direction does not discriminate; had they started at the stop vertex they would be a backward Michel and the verdict STM_MICHEL.

notes: ANODE: end at face.x 6.7 with no rise; the chain Michel pair (115040, 116015) is a ~3 cm low-charge hook at the wire plane, not clear topology; 115040 tagged muon as the straight-on continuation, 116015 delta / other
evidence: 418 cm track (0.97 GeV by range) running between the bottom face (chain entry at y 12.2, d_face 4.6) and the fit end at (351.3, 256.6, 433.4) in APA3: face.x 6.7, i.e. at the anode wire plane (|x| 351.3), 249 cm from the top/bottom, 29 cm from the back face and 202 cm from the seam. The track runs mostly along x (dx/ds ~0.78), so it meets the anode steeply, and in f_meas it ends at slice ~20, next to the anode, in all three planes. The dQ/dx holds a ~0.5-0.6e5 plateau with delta spikes; over the last 5 cm it stays at 0.4-0.6e5 and the last ~2 cm fall to 0.15-0.27e5 as the charge runs into the wire planes: no rise. At the end there is only a ~3 cm low-charge hook made of two tiny rows, 115040 (2.4 cm, 3 points, cos_fwd 0.92, carrying on into the anode) and 116015 (d 0-3.5, cos_fwd -0.62, 15k); with no rise and at the anode this is not clear decay topology, so it does not make a stop. Along the body there are ordinary deltas (116027 at 41 cm, 116012/116034/116035 70-230 cm back). A cosmic entering through the anode side wall and leaving through the bottom; the chain has the direction reversed, but both ends sit at faces.

notes: OVERSHOOT: peak 0.95-1.07e5 at 10-14 cm then a sustained 3.7-5e4 collapse over the last 6.5 cm; pin at 7.0 cm; collapse spans the end of 130001 and all of 130002. Competing reading: the fit end is the stop and the last 7 cm is a long low terminal dip; the verdict stays STM_MICHEL only through 130003, which in that reading attaches 4.5 cm back from the end.
evidence: Short straight downward track, 70 cm chord (72 cm chain), in APA3. Its upper end is 20 cm below the top (y 586, not at the face); the fit end is at x 247.7, y 532.5, z 332.9, 73.5 cm from the nearest face, 104 cm from the anode, 102 cm from the seam and 247 cm from the cathode. dy = -53.5 against 0.3 x chord = 21.1, so the fit end is the lower end (rule 7 silent). Profile: plateau 5.5-7e4 with humps to 8.6-9e4 at 22 and 40 cm; from 15 cm in it climbs to its highest values, 0.95-1.07e5 at 10-14 cm, holds 7-8.6e4 to 7.5 cm, and then collapses: every point from 6.5 cm to 1 cm reads 3.7-5e4, below the plateau, over about 12 points, with 5.8e4 at the last point. That is the lowest sustained stretch of the whole track, exactly where a muon at its Bragg peak would read 0.8-1.3e5 - the overshoot signature, not a single low end point. I put the true stop at the end of the peak, about 7 cm back, and read the collapsed last 7 cm as the start of the electron, carrying charge (not a gap). The fit bridges it straight on, so the rows split: 130001 (to 4.5 cm) is mostly muon with its last ~2.5 cm past the pin, and 130002 (last 4.8 cm, 4.8e4) is the electron. 130003 (5 cm, 1e4) branches from the 130001/130002 vertex, 2.4 cm past the new stop, and leaves the line at an angle in the c azimuth: part of the decay activity, michel. f_meas: the coloured charge ends in all three planes; a shallow grey track crosses the end in W only and crosses U 40 slices earlier, so it is a projection coincidence, not a continuation; V is clean; no dead band.

notes: Competing reading: a stopper with an unresolved Bragg peak (the 2-3 cm end spike) plus detached gammas 452033/451032 (kind detached dots). Held to medium by the unexplained 14.5 cm charge-free gap with no dead band in any plane, and the ~20 deg angle between the muon and the continuation line.
evidence: 182 cm, enters through the top 5.8 cm from y=606, fit end at (-36, 466, 109) in APA0, 109 cm from the nearest face, 33.5 cm from the cathode, 121.8 cm from the APA seam. The profile over 5-15 cm sits below its own APA0 plateau (~4-5e4) at 1-4e4, with a 2-3 cm spike to ~2x plateau only at the very end; the hump at 22-30 cm is at the junction of the attached arm 46010 (31-37 cm), not a Bragg peak. Nothing is attached at the stop: 46016 (2.5 cm, high charge) branches from the body vertex 4.9 cm back, on the body line. Past the stop there is a 14.5 cm charge-free gap with no hatched dead band in any plane, then 452033 (13 cm, d 14.5-24, cos_fwd 0.89, ~plateau charge) and 451032 (18.6 cm, d 37-52, cos_fwd 0.95) plus no-dqdx rows 30026/C123 at 51-60 cm, all on one line: their transverse offsets (8.7, 13.7, 20 cm) grow linearly with distance and extrapolate back to ~3 cm of the stop at ~16-26 deg to the muon direction. In f_meas the continuation is in all three planes within the window (U 790-800 collinear with the muon extrapolation, W 7130 running steeply in time to the cathode at ~1300), and faint context points continue the same line across the cathode to about (50, 350, 120) in both the side and end views, ~145 cm total - too long and straight for a gamma or electron. Read as one muon continuing into other clusters: FRAG_THRU. The forward pieces are the muon continuation but are tagged delta / other per the THRU tag rule; C31 is backward and degenerate.

notes: Near-isochronous track with patchy APA0 W charge: the end position is unreliable. Competing reading: a FLAT_STOP STM_ONLY at the fit end (charge ends in all planes, no dead band, mid-volume), which would require an upward-going muon; the direction argument and the isochronous exception hold this to medium.
evidence: 301 cm, the chain entry is at (-0.5, 321, 43), i.e. at the cathode, and the fit end is the UPPER end at (-27, 534, 203) in APA0, 72 cm below the top face, 24.6 cm from the cathode and 28.5 cm from the APA seam. The track is near-isochronous: x changes by only ~27 cm over 300 cm (about 5 deg to the anode plane), and it is sparsely imaged (386 image points over 300 cm). In f_meas the W measured charge exists only in patches (around 7160, 7215-7225, 7295-7305) with the predicted band continuing between them - the APA0 collection deficit / coverage pattern - and the dQ/dx panel is a smooth periodic modulation (peaks at ~5 and ~24 cm, troughs at ~10 and ~45 cm) that tracks those patches, not a Bragg rise: the last 5 cm fall from 7e4 to 3.5e4. Charge does end at the fit end in all three planes and nothing continues within the window, but rule 3 does not apply to a near-isochronous track. There are no other objects near the stop at all (four muon-chain rows only), so no decay activity. Also the fit end is the upper end of a track whose lower end sits at the cathode: for a downward cosmic this end is where it came in, not where it stopped. Called THRU.

notes: peak at s~6-8 cm then a 5 cm decline to plateau (not below): pin not moved; 298015 is a 2-point speck, weak gamma
evidence: 450 cm muon entering 2 cm below the top face (x 249, z 147), crossing the seam and stopping mid-volume in APA3 at (133, 263, 359): 103 cm from the back face, 255 cm above the floor, 133 cm from the cathode, 219 cm from the anode, 128 cm from the seam. dy = -341, the fit end is the lower end. dQ/dx: plateau ~55-60k beyond 40 cm; over the last ~15 cm it climbs to 85-95k (about 1.6x) peaking at s ~ 6-8 cm, then eases back to ~57-65k over the last 5 cm (the 5 cm chain piece 101017). That last stretch falls back to the plateau, not well below it, and 101017 carries on the curve of the muon smoothly in all three azimuths, so I read it as a smeared end, not an overshoot: pin left at the fit end (the competing reading would pin at s ~ 5). At the fit end a three-piece arm 101016 -> 101009 -> 101008 (about 11 cm of path, reaching 8.5 cm out) leaves at a sharp kink, clear in the d and e azimuths, at or below plateau charge (29-52k): the Michel. Three compact pieces 21-34 cm out lie on the Michel side (mostly -z, +y), ~9-11 cm clear of the body line in the 3-D views: 296013 (4.8 cm), 297014 (2.1 cm, right along the Michel direction), 298015 (2 points): gamma, the last two faint. 101006 is a delta ray 258 cm back on the body. f_meas: a V dead band sits at the V end, but U and W show the charge ending and turning into the Michel with no grey continuing the line.

blind.notes: peak at s~6-8 cm then a 5 cm decline to plateau (not below): pin not moved; 298015 is a 2-point speck, weak gamma

notes: U dead band at the stop end, V and W clean; no Bragg rise (wavy profile), verdict from the kinked plateau-charge arm
evidence: 94 cm steep track in APA1 (x 55-66, z 120-134): enters 8.3 cm below the top face, runs down and stops mid-volume at y=511, 95 cm below the top, 286 cm from the anode, 66 cm from the cathode, 97 cm from the seam. Direction: dy = -87, the fit end is the lower end, as a down-going cosmic should be. dQ/dx: the body is a regular wave between 40k and 80k around a ~55k plateau; the last 3 cm are at 70-75k, which is one crest of that wave, so no clear Bragg rise. Topology decides: 117008 (11.7 cm, d_min 0, cos_fwd 0.27) leaves the stop vertex at a sharp kink (~75 deg), clearly visible in the d and e azimuths; its charge is at plateau (54.5k, points 35-80k, falling to ~6-35k at its far end), not the 2-3x a muon at its Bragg peak would carry, so it is a second particle: michel. Not a hot tip (charge not several times plateau, not straight ahead). Two compact specks 387009 (2.8 cm, 21 cm out) and 388010 (3.4 cm, 29 cm out) lie below the stop, clear of the body line, both within ~30 deg of the Michel direction (mostly -x, -y): gamma. f_meas: the track and arm end in all three planes; U has a dead band covering the last ~15 channels of the track, but V and W show the charge ending cleanly with no grey continuing along the line; the grey tracks nearby cross the region in other directions.

blind.notes: U dead band at the stop end, V and W clean; no Bragg rise (wavy profile), verdict from the kinked plateau-charge arm

notes: NO_MEASUREMENT: the track is too sparsely imaged (runs along a dead W band, internal 17 cm hole, whole profile below MIP) to read a Bragg rise, and the upper end is also truncated, so rule 3 cannot be trusted. Competing reading: FLAT_STOP STM_ONLY (charge ends in all planes mid-volume, no Michel).
evidence: 55 cm, a nearly vertical track at almost constant z (~245-252); its upper (chain entry) end floats at y=586.5, 19.5 cm below the top face, so it was not imaged all the way in. The fit end is at (183, 539, 245) in APA3, 67 cm from the nearest face, 13.8 cm from the APA seam, 181 cm from the cathode. Only 107 image points: the charge comes in two pieces (0-15 cm and 32-55 cm) with a ~17 cm hole between, and the whole dQ/dx profile is far below a MIP plateau (<=4e4, falling to ~0 at 37 cm); the smooth climb from 1e4 at 15 cm to 4e4 at the end is interpolation over sparse charge, not a Bragg rise. In f_meas the track runs along a hatched dead W band (9305-9310) and W measured exists only at the lower end (9315-9322); U and V show measured charge only in two small blobs. At the fit end charge does stop in all three planes and nothing continues within the window, but the same kind of truncation happened at the upper end, where a downward cosmic certainly existed, so an end of charge here does not demonstrate a stop. evidence: 95 cm chain in APA0; upper end at (x -85, y 174, z 15.5), 15 cm from the front face, fit end at (-104.8, 117.2, 51.8), 51.5 cm from the front face, 102 cm from the cathode and 179 cm from the seam. dQ/dx is wavy: 3-8.5e4 over 20-45 cm, a bump to 8.2e4 at 22 cm, then the last ~17 cm (the final segment 32001, avg 2.5e4) stays low: near-zero at 10-13 cm, a 2.8e4 hump at 6 cm, 1.3-1.8e4 over the last 4 cm. evidence: 294 cm track entering through the top (face.y 5.3) and stopping mid-volume at (-128.9, 350.1, 329.0) in APA2 (not its bottom corner): 133 cm from the nearest face, 126 cm from the cathode, 98 cm from the APA seam.
